entities.name: Diego Núñez de Avendaño
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Diego Núñez de Avendaño (1512–c. 1595) was a Spanish jurist and legal scholar who made significant contributions to colonial law — the legal system governing Spain's American empire. His major work was a treatise on the authority and jurisdiction of Spanish colonial officials — the visitadores and other royal inspectors — that became a standard reference for understanding the legal framework of colonial governance.

The Spanish colonial legal system was one of the most elaborate in history — a complex body of law combining Castilian law, Roman law, canon law, and specifically American decrees that governed the relationship between the Crown, colonial officials, settlers, indigenous people, and the Church.

Núñez de Avendaño worked within the tradition of Spanish scholastic jurisprudence — the legal scholars who combined Thomist theology, Roman law, and royal decrees into a comprehensive system of colonial governance.

He contributed to the development of Spanish colonial law.
